cd /workspace && cat > submission/README.md <<'EOF'
# Synecdoche discovery-to-deployment project (contract v3.0)

`run.py` is the single-request entry point: it reads one UTF-8 JSON object from
stdin to EOF and writes exactly one JSON object to stdout.  Valid requests
produce the certificate/replay document; every syntax, schema, bound or
lifecycle violation produces `{"error":"invalid_request"}`.  Both paths exit 0
and never emit partial certificates.  Offline CPU only: NumPy, SciPy and the
pinned scikit-learn 1.4.2 tree path from `wheels/manifest.json` (located
through `SYNECDOCHE_SITE`), no capture, training, network or switch hardware.

## Module map

| file | contract area |
| --- | --- |
| `formats.py` | strict JSON tokens, container bounds, schema and aggregate budgets |
| `offline_discovery/rule_generate.py` | real prefix, high-activation runs, fragments, anchored distance, clustering, generalized intervals |
| `offline_discovery/rule_remove.py` | validation coverage, exact scores, keep filter, shared priority, exact key census |
| `online_matching/train_rf.py` | pinned `DecisionTreeClassifier` backup, node-order certificate, integer prediction rule |
| `online_matching/match_p4.py` | resident bank entry pools and the per-length segment tables |
| `sessions.py` | atomic installs, bank pins, flow epochs, packet/idle/limit/close commitments |
| `pipeline.py` | glue: derive fragments, budget check, calibrate, build banks, replay |

## Exactness

Everything the contract calls mathematical is computed with integers:

* a position is high iff `n*value - sum > 0` and `(n*value - sum)^2 > n*sumsq - sum^2`
  (population sigma, no floating point);
* the neighbourhood test `sqrt(S/L)*(3/5)^A <= eps` is decided as the integer
  comparison `S*q^2*3^(2A) <= p^2*L*5^(2A)`.  A vectorised float pass only
  pre-filters; cells inside a `1e-9` relative band are re-decided exactly, so
  `eps` equality (for example `sqrt(49/9)*3/5 = 1.4`) is honoured;
* interval bounds use `isqrt` on `m*sum(x^2) - sum(x)^2`, so
  `trunc(lo-sigma)` needs `ceil(sigma)` and `trunc(hi+sigma)` needs
  `floor(sigma)` exactly before clamping to `[0,3028]`;
* coverage, scores (`Cin/(Cout+1/10000)`), the `score > threshold` keep test and
  the priority order use `Fraction`; output fractions are reduced.
* the backup certificate stores `2*threshold` as an integer and replay walks the
  certificate itself (`left iff 2*feature <= 2*threshold`), so table and replay
  can never disagree.

## Cost model

* Clustering is per class and length.  Pairwise neighbourhoods come from the
  identity that the contract distance is Euclidean on the transformed values
  (`v>1514` gains 1000), computed block-wise, so 4096 fragments in one group are
  sub-second.
* Validation coverage is one bitwise sweep per row per pattern length: each
  coordinate holds a coverage bitmask per value, so cost is independent of the
  number of patterns up to a word factor.
* Segment tables index the tightest coordinate with a CSR of candidates in
  priority order, so a packet inspects only the patterns that coordinate admits
  and the first surviving candidate is the highest-priority match across lengths.
* Exact bank keys are never enumerated when one box already exceeds the pool;
  identical boxes are merged and contained boxes dropped before the census stops
  at `capacity.exact + 1`.

The published maximum request (218432 operations, 200000 packets, 8192 epochs,
4096 fragments, ~1M values, 2048 installs) completes in a few seconds of CPU and
well under the 1GiB address space.

## Development

From `/workspace`: `python3 check.py submission` prepares the supplied wheels
offline and replays the public fixtures through bounded children.  The graded
suite is larger; the public fixtures are sanity checks only.
EOF
